title: Member Services Guidance Note: COBRA Continuation under Employer Group Contracts
content:
**Rule.** When COBRA applies to the group's Cascade Group Dental & Vision segment, an employee or dependent losing coverage under an Employer Group Contract because employment ended or hours were reduced may elect continuation within the election window after the later of coverage loss and the election notice; continuation lasts the continuation period (the disability total with a disability determination, the secondary-event total for dependents after a second qualifying event). The election window is counted in calendar days from the later of the coverage-loss date and the election notice date, and an election on the last day is timely. The first premium is due within the initial premium period after the election and later premiums have the subsequent grace period; the premium is the continuation premium percentage of the group rate. The employer must notify Cascade within the employer notice period; groups where COBRA does not apply offer no continuation under these rules.

## Figures used by the rule

| Term | Figure in every segment where COBRA applies |
|---|---|
| Election window | 60 calendar days |
| Continuation period | 18 months |
| Total with a disability determination | 29 months |
| Total for dependents after a second qualifying event | 36 months |
| First premium due | within 45 calendar days after the election |
| Grace for each later premium | 30 calendar days |
| Continuation premium | 102 percent of the group rate |
| Employer notice to Cascade | within 30 calendar days |

## The election window

- **Records relied on.** The coverage-loss date is the coverage end date on the company's record of the reported termination that the election continues; it is read from that record, not from the caller's account, before the election is recorded, and the election is recorded against that termination.
- **Start of the count.** The later of the coverage-loss date and the election notice date.
- **Length and counting.** 60 calendar days added to that date gives the last day of the window.
- **Boundary.** An election on the last day is timely; an election on the day after the last day falls outside the window.

| Hypothetical coverage-loss date | Hypothetical election notice date | Count runs from | Last day of the window | Election on that last day | Election on the following day |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| April 30 | May 10 | May 10 | July 9 | timely | outside the window |
| April 30 | April 20 | April 30 | June 29 | timely | outside the window |

## What an election records

An election records the employee, the coverage tier continued, the date coverage was lost, the continuation start date, which is the day after coverage ended, and the election date. In the first row above, with coverage ending April 30, continuation starts on May 1.

## Premium (hypothetical rate)

With a hypothetical group rate of 52.50 dollars for the tier continued, the continuation premium at 102 percent of the group rate is 53.55 dollars.
